Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"

Use claude-mem for your own durable notes. For server notes, use observation_add for the selected server project when available; save_memory is local-worker only. Use only tools and argument names advertised by the active connection; no auto or guided modes.
Use work_state_write for to-do lists and changing work state when available. Keep durable notes concise, distinguish verified facts from guesses, and exclude credentials and private material the user asked you not to remember. Native memory files can remain enabled; an explicitly configured memory folder watcher imports their Markdown notes into claude-mem. Never assume a hosted memory search was intercepted: search claude-mem directly when its result is needed.

1: # Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions
2: 
3: These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:
4: 
5: - a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
6: - full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
7: - `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
8: - HEAD moved during a pause.
9: 
10: They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.
11: 
12: ## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent
13: 
14: - The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
15: - An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
16: - An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.
17: 
18: ## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)
19: 
20: Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.
21: 
22: ```sh
23: CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
24: mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
25: SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
26: if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
27:   printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
28:     "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
29: else
30:   echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
31: fi
32: ```
33: 
34: - **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
35: - **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
36: - **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
37: - If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.
38: 
39: ## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes
40: 
41: | Resource | Rule |
42: |---|---|
43: | Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
44: | Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
45: | HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
46: | Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
47: | Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
48: | Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
49: | Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
50: | Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
51: | Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |
52: 
53: ## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly
54: 
55: These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.
56: 
57: | File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
58: |---|---|---|
59: | `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
60: | `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
61: | `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
62: | `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
63: | `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
64: | `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
65: | `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
66: | `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
67: | `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
68: | `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
69: | `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
70: | `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
71: | `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
72: | `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |
73: | `harness.sh`, `install.sh`, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `.github/workflows/*` | 05, 06, 07, 09, C1 | Claim required. Workflow edits are separate commits. |
74: | `cli/dist/**` | all, while tracked | Do not commit `cli/dist` from slices. PLAN-07 PR-7d untracks it (DEC-10). Until that merges, only the merging agent rebuilds and commits dist, in a final separate commit, after rebasing. |
75: | `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md`, `quickstart.md` | 05, 09 and doc tasks in every plan | Edit only the sections your slice changes. Hold a short `FILE_` claim. |
76: 
77: ### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)
78: 
79: A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.
80: 
81: ## 5. Commit and merge discipline
82: 
83: 1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
84: 2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
85: 3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
86: 4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
87: 5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
88: 6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.
89: 
90: ## 6. Coordination records
91: 
92: | Record | Where | Purpose |
93: |---|---|---|
94: | Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
95: | Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
96: | Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
97: | Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |
98: 
99: ## 7. Safe parallel lanes

## 5. Architectural Invariants Across All Post-v1 Releases

1. **Security & Boundary Preservation:** No post-v1 observability or evaluation feature may bypass or weaken the v1.0.0 security boundaries (untrusted `.env` rejection, SSRF blocking, container path confinement, or workspace trust).
2. **Local Sovereignty:** Nexus remains 100% operational in air-gapped, offline, and self-hosted environments. External network transmission of telemetry is disabled by default and strictly opt-in.
3. **Open Standards:** Telemetry formats conform to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions rather than proprietary vendor SDKs.
4. **Reproducibility:** All benchmark datasets, evaluator code, and comparison tools are committed directly to the repository and execute deterministically under isolated `$HOME`.
5. **Zero Technical Debt & Zero Deprecated Packages (Inviolable Invariant):**
   - Strictly **NO deprecated packages or unmaintained third-party library dependencies** may ever be introduced, merged, or retained in any component or release—ever.
   - Every npm dependency and Cargo crate must be on active, supported upstream releases.
   - Automated CI gates fail closed on:
     - Any npm package marked `deprecated` by the npm registry (`npm audit` and package-tree deprecation scans).
     - Any Rust crate flagged as unmaintained, yanked, or deprecated in the RustSec advisory database (`cargo deny check bans advisories`).
   - *Platform engines vs. libraries:* Platform runtime engine requirements (such as Node.js) follow explicit project architectural decisions (DEC-12), with upstream EOL status disclosed and modern LTS versions recommended.
   - When upstream library dependencies announce deprecation or breaking lifecycles, Nexus must refactor, migrate, or replace them before minor release qualification. Under no circumstances may technical debt be deferred into permanent legacy layers.
6. **Opt-In External Integrations & Boundary Invariant:**
   - All third-party services and app connectors (including Composio developer bridges and enterprise app toolsets) are strictly **opt-in** and disabled by default.
   - Nexus Code must always retain 100% operational capability in air-gapped, zero-network environments without external API keys.
   - External tokens (`NEXUS_COMPOSIO_API_KEY`) must never be leaked into git commits, trace logs, or flight recordings (`CRED003`).
   - High-impact or state-mutating actions on external services require explicit operator confirmation prompts before execution.

1: # Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions
2: 
3: These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:
4: 
5: - a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
6: - full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
7: - `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
8: - HEAD moved during a pause.
9: 
10: They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.
11: 
12: ## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent
13: 
14: - The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
15: - An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
16: - An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.
17: 
18: ## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)
19: 
20: Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.
21: 
22: ```sh
23: CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
24: mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
25: SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
26: if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
27:   printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
28:     "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
29: else
30:   echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
31: fi
32: ```
33: 
34: - **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
35: - **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
36: - **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
37: - If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.
38: 
39: ## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes
40: 
41: | Resource | Rule |
42: |---|---|
43: | Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
44: | Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
45: | HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
46: | Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
47: | Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
48: | Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
49: | Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
50: | Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
51: | Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |
52: 
53: ## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly
54: 
55: These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.
56: 
57: | File | Plans that touch it | Rule |

59: | `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
60: | `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |

77: ### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)
78: 
79: A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

81: ## 5. Commit and merge discipline
82: 
83: 1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).

# Deterministic code evaluators (WP-1105)

Dependency-free scoring helpers for hard code checks. Every helper returns the same envelope,
`{ evaluator, passed, score, details }`. They never call a model, and they never infer success from task metadata or
from what the agent said about its own work.

- **`syntax_ast.mjs`**
  - Parses each modified file with a real parser.
  - The built-in parsers in `parsers.mjs` need nothing beyond the host's Node.js and Python:
    - **TypeScript** (`.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`): Node's own TypeScript parser (`module.stripTypeScriptTypes`, transform
      mode). Requires Node.js 22.13 or later.
    - **JavaScript** (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`): `node --check` on the file, so the module type is decided exactly as
      Node would decide it.
    - **Python** (`.py`): `ast.parse` in an isolated interpreter.
  - Rust, TSX and JSX have no built-in parser. A caller can supply one for any language, or replace a built-in one.
  - Fails closed on: a language with no parser, an unsupported extension, an unreadable file, a path that is
    absolute, contains traversal, or escapes the workspace through a symlink, and an empty file list.
- **`build.mjs`**
  - Runs an explicit command and argv through `command.mjs`: `spawnSync` with no shell, a minimal environment and a
    timeout.
  - Passes only on exit status 0 with no timeout, signal or spawn error.
- **`typecheck_clean.mjs`**
  - Runs the baseline and candidate typecheck commands in separate workspaces.
  - Fails on any diagnostic line the candidate adds; existing diagnostics may remain. Duplicate lines are counted.
  - Also fails when the candidate exits non-zero and either the baseline exited 0 or the candidate printed nothing.
  - A spawn failure, timeout or signal on either side fails closed.
  - The comparison is exact, so callers should normalize paths that differ between revisions.
- **`diff_boundary.mjs`**
  - Checks Git-style relative paths against exact allowed paths and directory prefixes ending in `/`.
  - Absolute paths, traversal, empty or `.` segments, NUL bytes and backslashes fail closed.
- **`json_repair_rate.mjs`**
  - Scores the agent's own tool-call syntax telemetry: the `toolCallSyntax` counts on each turn result
    (`nexus run --json` → `turn.toolCallSyntax`).
  - Scoring: native JSON is 1, JSON recovered by a trailing or structural repair is 0.5, and arguments that did not
    parse are 0.
  - Any invalid call fails the result. So does having no tool calls recorded, since there is nothing to score.
  - The counts come from the parser and cover every tool call it recognizes, including structurally repaired write
    calls that are rejected.

### 4.1 Deterministic Code Evaluators (`eval/evaluators/code/`)
Deterministic evaluators check hard invariants without calling LLMs. They are fast, reproducible, and free of grading variance:
1. **`syntax_ast.ts`:** Validates TypeScript/JavaScript/Rust/Python syntax across modified files using standard language parsers (`oxc`, `syn`, `tree-sitter`).
2. **`typecheck_clean.ts`:** Executes language typecheckers (`tsc --noEmit`, `cargo check`) and ensures 0 new diagnostics.
3. **`diff_boundary.ts`:** Enforces safe change boundaries by asserting that `git diff --name-only` contains only allowed paths.
4. **`json_repair_rate.ts`:** Evaluates tool call parser telemetry, scoring 1.0 for valid native JSON and 0.5 for recovered malformed JSON.
5. **`secret_leak_check.ts`:** Asserts 0 occurrences of API keys, private tokens, or unredacted credentials across all output files and logs.

### 4.1 Code Evaluators (Deterministic)

Rule-based functions that check structural properties:
- Output is not empty
- Generated code compiles
- Classification matches exactly
- JSON structure is valid

**Nexus parallel:** `repairJson` validation, `isKnownToolName` checks, `ALL_DIGITS_RE` validation. These are already implicit code evaluators but could be formalized as first-class evaluator functions with named scores.

### 4.2 LLM-as-Judge

LLMs score outputs based on criteria encoded in prompts:
- **Reference-free:** Toxicity detection, clarity, helpfulness, tone
- **Reference-based:** Factual accuracy, semantic similarity to reference

**Relevance to Nexus:** Nexus could use LLM-as-judge to score whether a tool call's output actually satisfies the user's intent, even when no exact reference output exists. This is valuable for open-ended tasks where exact-match evaluation is too strict.

### 4.3 Human Evaluation

Manual review of outputs and traces. LangSmith provides:
- **Annotation queues:** Structured review of runs against rubrics
- **Single-run queues:** Review one run at a time with custom rubric items
- **Pairwise queues:** Compare two runs side-by-side to judge which is better

**Relevance to Nexus:** Nexus's independent acceptance review (X5) currently reviews samples manually. Annotation queues would formalize this with rubric items, multi-reviewer support, and export of annotated runs back into the eval dataset.

### 4.4 Decision Model Evaluators

Typed questions (probability true/false, choice from fixed list, score along ordered levels) instead of free-form prompts.

1: # WP-1106: Single-step agent loop mode
2: 
3: ## Specification draft
4: 
5: **Decision for this draft:** Interpret “one agent turn and pause” as one bounded model/tool cycle: one provider response and every tool call returned in that response are handled, then Nexus pauses before making another provider request. A user-level `/step` command advances an existing unresolved objective by one such cycle; it is an operator command, not another prompt and not a new full `runTurn`.
6: 
7: **User story:** As an operator supervising an autonomous task, I need to advance the same task one model/tool cycle at a time, so I can inspect durable progress and explicitly authorize the next cycle.
8: 
9: **Acceptance criteria (binary, testable):**
10: 
11: - **AC1:** `nexus run --step <prompt>` makes at most one provider request cycle, executes all tool calls returned by that response, records a resumable paused result when the task remains unresolved, and issues no second provider request. Test: `run --step pauses after one model-tool cycle`.
12: - **AC2:** `/step` in the REPL advances the current unresolved objective by exactly one cycle, returns control to the REPL prompt, and does not append or amend a user prompt. Test: `/step advances the current objective by exactly one cycle`.
13: - **AC3:** A paused one-shot task resumes by running `nexus run --resume --step`; a paused REPL task resumes by launching the REPL with its existing session via `nexus --resume [id]` and issuing `/step`. Both paths advance exactly one cycle from durable state; previously completed tool calls are not replayed and the original objective and conversation remain present. Tests: `run --resume --step resumes durable state without replaying completed tools`; `/step resumes saved objective after REPL restart`.
14: - **AC4:** A terminal model result completes normally without a false paused status; cancellation, approval wait, provider failure, and persistence failure retain their existing classifications and are not rewritten as a normal pause. Test: `step mode preserves terminal and interrupted outcomes`.
15: - **AC5:** Default `nexus run`, normal REPL prompts, and current segment/continuation behavior remain unchanged unless the operator explicitly selects step mode. Test: `step mode is opt-in and leaves default continuation unchanged`.
16: 
17: **Out of scope:** Applying step mode to `/team`, nested subagents, operation runners, or the live TUI; redesigning turn budgets or durable operation schemas; changing approval policy; automatically continuing after a pause.
18: 
19: **Dependencies:** No WP feature dependency identified. The design relies on the current durable objective/session state and REPL persistence contracts. Confirm compatibility with active PR398 changes to `cli/src/agent.ts` before implementation. This work must not weaken v1.0.0 completion, verification, approval, or persistence invariants.
20: 
21: ## Plan
22: 
23: 1. **Bound a model/tool cycle in the agent loop** — files: `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/test/objective_continuation.test.ts`, `cli/test/durable_continuity.test.ts`; test: `run --step pauses after one model-tool cycle`. Add an explicit opt-in cycle bound separate from `maxSteps` (which currently bounds a durable segment and can continue across segments). Use a deterministic local gateway to return multiple tool-call responses and prove the first response's full tool batch finishes before pause and the second response is not requested.
24: 2. **One-shot command and durable resume** — files: `cli/src/index.ts`, `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/test/run_json_output.test.ts`, `cli/test/objective_continuation.test.ts`; tests: `run --resume --step resumes durable state without replaying completed tools`, `step mode is opt-in and leaves default continuation unchanged`. Define the JSON/text paused result and the exact `nexus run --resume --step` path; verify objective, transcript, tool receipts, and completion status survive a fresh process. Include restart after a completed tool batch and a crash during an in-flight tool, preserving existing recovery semantics.
25: 3. **REPL `/step` operator control and lifecycle outcomes** — files: `cli/src/repl.ts`, `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/test/repl_readonly_e2e.test.ts`, `cli/test/durable_continuity.test.ts`; tests: `/step advances the current objective by exactly one cycle`, `/step resumes saved objective after REPL restart`, `step mode preserves terminal and interrupted outcomes`. Route `/step` as a built-in command that resumes the stored unresolved objective with the one-cycle bound, returns to the prompt, and errors clearly if no unresolved objective exists. It must not send `/step` text to the model or amend the objective. Verify a saved task survives process restart and one more `/step` advances it without replay; terminal completion, cancellation, approval wait, provider failure, and persistence failure preserve their existing classifications and are not rewritten as a normal pause.
26: 
27: ## Reference and source observations
28: 
29: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, definition `runTurn`: `agent.ts:5241`; method accepts a prompt, confirmation handler, and options including signal/resume/TDD mode.
30: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, definition `startRepl`: `index.ts:204`; existing REPL setup boundary.
31: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, natural-language search for REPL turn dispatch: `repl.ts:186`; `runInteractiveTurn` calls `agent.runTurn` and installs a progress listener.
32: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, command-registration search: `index.ts:2`; Commander-based CLI registration context.
33: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-test`, deterministic loop search: `objective_continuation.test.ts:3`; tests exercise the real agent loop against a deterministic local gateway.
34: - Source inspection (origin/main at `593d569b5aa2a43d1b31138d37e90b8b65ffcbe7`): `agent.ts:5367` persists the durable objective/user prompt before provider work; `agent.ts:5814` persists tool-call messages before tools execute; `agent.ts:5866` persists tool outputs after the batch; `repl.ts:187-193` saves the current session on progress and synchronously saves at turn end. `agent.ts:5410` documents that `maxSteps` bounds a durable segment and default continuation may continue beyond it, so `--max-steps 1` alone does not implement this contract.
35: 
36: ## Risks and required plan review
37: 
38: - **Semantic risk:** The source currently defines `runTurn` as the whole user task loop, with multiple provider/tool cycles. This draft treats the roadmap's “one agent turn” as one cycle within that loop. The owner must approve this interpretation before implementation; if existing product language or durable-operation semantics require a complete `runTurn`, revise AC1/AC2 rather than silently changing the meaning.
39: - **Partial-cycle lifecycle risk:** Current code distinguishes terminal model text, malformed/empty replies, cancellation, confirmation waits, provider recovery and persistence failure. The bounded loop must pause only after a fully persisted, resumable cycle and preserve those classifications. Resume is explicit: `nexus run --resume --step` for one-shot mode; restart the REPL with its saved session (`nexus --resume [id]`) and then issue `/step` for interactive mode.
40: - **Shared-file claims:** `cli/src/agent.ts` is currently held by claude-code for PR398 non-progress recovery; `cli/src/index.ts` is held by the WP-1104 integration slice. Coordinate exact-hunk/file-claim handoff before implementation. Plan-file claim only: `docs/v1.1.0/WP-1106-PLAN.md`.
41: - **Plan review gate:** Independent review is complete and `APPROVED`. Phase 3 retrieval for newly discovered APIs and Phase 4 implementation/tests can proceed only after the parent assigns the slice and conflicting source-file claims are coordinated.

1: # WP-1106: Single-step agent loop mode
2: 
3: ## Specification draft
4: 
5: **Decision for this draft:** Interpret “one agent turn and pause” as one bounded model/tool cycle: one provider response and every tool call returned in that response are handled, then Nexus pauses before making another provider request. A user-level `/step` command advances an existing unresolved objective by one such cycle; it is an operator command, not another prompt and not a new full `runTurn`.
6: 
7: **User story:** As an operator supervising an autonomous task, I need to advance the same task one model/tool cycle at a time, so I can inspect durable progress and explicitly authorize the next cycle.
8: 
9: **Acceptance criteria (binary, testable):**
10: 
11: - **AC1:** `nexus run --step <prompt>` makes at most one provider request cycle, executes all tool calls returned by that response, records a resumable paused result when the task remains unresolved, and issues no second provider request. Test: `run --step pauses after one model-tool cycle`.
12: - **AC2:** `/step` in the REPL advances the current unresolved objective by exactly one cycle, returns control to the REPL prompt, and does not append or amend a user prompt. Test: `/step advances the current objective by exactly one cycle`.
13: - **AC3:** A paused one-shot task resumes by running `nexus run --resume --step`; a paused REPL task resumes by launching the REPL with its existing session via `nexus --resume [id]` and issuing `/step`. Both paths advance exactly one cycle from durable state; previously completed tool calls are not replayed and the original objective and conversation remain present. Tests: `run --resume --step resumes durable state without replaying completed tools`; `/step resumes saved objective after REPL restart`.
14: - **AC4:** A terminal model result completes normally without a false paused status; cancellation, approval wait, provider failure, and persistence failure retain their existing classifications and are not rewritten as a normal pause. Test: `step mode preserves terminal and interrupted outcomes`.
15: - **AC5:** Default `nexus run`, normal REPL prompts, and current segment/continuation behavior remain unchanged unless the operator explicitly selects step mode. Test: `step mode is opt-in and leaves default continuation unchanged`.
16: 
17: **Out of scope:** Applying step mode to `/team`, nested subagents, operation runners, or the live TUI; redesigning turn budgets or durable operation schemas; changing approval policy; automatically continuing after a pause.
18: 
19: **Dependencies:** No WP feature dependency identified. The design relies on the current durable objective/session state and REPL persistence contracts. Confirm compatibility with active PR398 changes to `cli/src/agent.ts` before implementation. This work must not weaken v1.0.0 completion, verification, approval, or persistence invariants.
20: 
21: ## Plan
22: 
23: 1. **Bound a model/tool cycle in the agent loop** — files: `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/test/objective_continuation.test.ts`, `cli/test/durable_continuity.test.ts`; test: `run --step pauses after one model-tool cycle`. Add an explicit opt-in cycle bound separate from `maxSteps` (which currently bounds a durable segment and can continue across segments). Use a deterministic local gateway to return multiple tool-call responses and prove the first response's full tool batch finishes before pause and the second response is not requested.
24: 2. **One-shot command and durable resume** — files: `cli/src/index.ts`, `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/test/run_json_output.test.ts`, `cli/test/objective_continuation.test.ts`; tests: `run --resume --step resumes durable state without replaying completed tools`, `step mode is opt-in and leaves default continuation unchanged`. Define the JSON/text paused result and the exact `nexus run --resume --step` path; verify objective, transcript, tool receipts, and completion status survive a fresh process. Include restart after a completed tool batch and a crash during an in-flight tool, preserving existing recovery semantics.
25: 3. **REPL `/step` operator control and lifecycle outcomes** — files: `cli/src/repl.ts`, `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/test/repl_readonly_e2e.test.ts`, `cli/test/durable_continuity.test.ts`; tests: `/step advances the current objective by exactly one cycle`, `/step resumes saved objective after REPL restart`, `step mode preserves terminal and interrupted outcomes`. Route `/step` as a built-in command that resumes the stored unresolved objective with the one-cycle bound, returns to the prompt, and errors clearly if no unresolved objective exists. It must not send `/step` text to the model or amend the objective. Verify a saved task survives process restart and one more `/step` advances it without replay; terminal completion, cancellation, approval wait, provider failure, and persistence failure preserve their existing classifications and are not rewritten as a normal pause.
26: 
27: ## Reference and source observations
28: 
29: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, definition `runTurn`: `agent.ts:5241`; method accepts a prompt, confirmation handler, and options including signal/resume/TDD mode.
30: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, definition `startRepl`: `index.ts:204`; existing REPL setup boundary.
31: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, natural-language search for REPL turn dispatch: `repl.ts:186`; `runInteractiveTurn` calls `agent.runTurn` and installs a progress listener.
32: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-cli`, command-registration search: `index.ts:2`; Commander-based CLI registration context.
33: - XERJ retrieval — corpus `nexus-test`, deterministic loop search: `objective_continuation.test.ts:3`; tests exercise the real agent loop against a deterministic local gateway.
34: - Source inspection (origin/main at `593d569b5aa2a43d1b31138d37e90b8b65ffcbe7`): `agent.ts:5367` persists the durable objective/user prompt before provider work; `agent.ts:5814` persists tool-call messages before tools execute; `agent.ts:5866` persists tool outputs after the batch; `repl.ts:187-193` saves the current session on progress and synchronously saves at turn end. `agent.ts:5410` documents that `maxSteps` bounds a durable segment and default continuation may continue beyond it, so `--max-steps 1` alone does not implement this contract.
35: 
36: ## Risks and required plan review
37: 
38: - **Semantic risk:** The source currently defines `runTurn` as the whole user task loop, with multiple provider/tool cycles. This draft treats the roadmap's “one agent turn” as one cycle within that loop. The owner must approve this interpretation before implementation; if existing product language or durable-operation semantics require a complete `runTurn`, revise AC1/AC2 rather than silently changing the meaning.
39: - **Partial-cycle lifecycle risk:** Current code distinguishes terminal model text, malformed/empty replies, cancellation, confirmation waits, provider recovery and persistence failure. The bounded loop must pause only after a fully persisted, resumable cycle and preserve those classifications. Resume is explicit: `nexus run --resume --step` for one-shot mode; restart the REPL with its saved session (`nexus --resume [id]`) and then issue `/step` for interactive mode.
40: - **Shared-file claims:** `cli/src/agent.ts` is currently held by claude-code for PR398 non-progress recovery; `cli/src/index.ts` is held by the WP-1104 integration slice. Coordinate exact-hunk/file-claim handoff before implementation. Plan-file claim only: `docs/v1.1.0/WP-1106-PLAN.md`.
41: - **Plan review gate:** Independent review is complete and `APPROVED`. Phase 3 retrieval for newly discovered APIs and Phase 4 implementation/tests can proceed only after the parent assigns the slice and conflicting source-file claims are coordinated.

13: ## 1. Objective
14: 
15: Provide Nexus Code with a structured, standards-compliant observability and evaluation layer that enables:
16: 1. **Hierarchical Execution Visibility:** Real-time and retrospective inspection of agent turns, model calls, tool executions, and context compaction.
17: 2. **Local-First Privacy:** Zero network egress of prompt text, source code, or credentials by default.
18: 3. **OpenTelemetry Interoperability:** Conformance with OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions (`v1.27.0+`), allowing pluggable export to Jaeger, SigNoz, Langfuse, or LangSmith.
19: 4. **Structured Evaluation:** Versioned datasets with strict separation of agent stimulus (`examples.jsonl`) from evaluation assertions (`oracles.jsonl`).
20: 5. **Deterministic Replay:** Containerized reproduction of tool call sequences without re-invoking inference models.
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 2. OpenTelemetry GenAI Span Architecture
25: 
26: Every agent execution is modeled as a tree of OpenTelemetry-compatible spans:
27: 
28: ```
29: [Trace: Agent Session (Thread)]
30:  └── [Span: Turn 1 (Root)]
31:       ├── [Span: Model Inference Request] (gen_ai.system=openai, model=qwen2.5-coder)
32:       ├── [Span: Tool Invocation: read_file] (agent.tool.name=read_file, path=cli/src/agent.ts)
33:       ├── [Span: Tool Invocation: run_command] (agent.tool.name=run_command, cmd=npm test)
34:       │    └── [Event: Process Spawned] (pid=45812)
35:       │    └── [Event: Process Exited] (exit_code=0)
36:       ├── [Span: Context Compaction] (nexus.compaction.reason=token_ceiling)
37:       └── [Span: Model Inference Request] (gen_ai.system=openai, model=qwen2.5-coder)
38: ```
39: 
40: ### 2.1 Span Specifications
41: 
42: #### Turn Span (Root)
43: - **Name:** `nexus.agent.turn`
44: - **Kind:** `INTERNAL`
45: - **Attributes:**
46:   - `nexus.turn.id`: UUIDv4
47:   - `nexus.session.id`: Current session UUID
48:   - `nexus.turn.objective`: User prompt / objective string (redacted)
49:   - `nexus.turn.step_count`: Total steps executed
50:   - `nexus.turn.outcome`: `SUCCESS` | `FAILED` | `CANCELLED` | `PERSISTENCE_FAILED`
51:   - `nexus.turn.duration_ms`: Wall-clock execution time in milliseconds
52: 
53: #### Model Inference Span
54: - **Name:** `gen_ai.client.chat`
55: - **Kind:** `CLIENT`
56: - **Attributes (OTel Standard):**
57:   - `gen_ai.system`: Provider classification (`openai`, `vllm`, `anthropic`, `ollama`)
58:   - `gen_ai.request.model`: Requested model name
59:   - `gen_ai.response.model`: Actual model returned by endpoint
60:   - `gen_ai.request.temperature`: Temperature float
61:   - `gen_ai.request.max_tokens`: Configured output token limit
62:   - `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`: Measured or estimated prompt tokens
63:   - `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`: Measured completion tokens
64:   - `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`: `["stop"]` | `["tool_calls"]` | `["length"]`
65:   - `nexus.inference.endpoint`: Base URL of inference endpoint (with credentials stripped)
66:   - `nexus.inference.token_accounting_mode`: `STRICT_MEASURED` | `CLIENT_ESTIMATE`
67: 
68: #### Tool Execution Span
69: - **Name:** `nexus.tool.execute`
70: - **Kind:** `INTERNAL`
71: - **Attributes:**
72:   - `agent.tool.name`: Registered tool name (e.g. `run_command`, `read_file`, `edit_file`)
73:   - `agent.tool.parameters`: JSON-stringified sanitized parameters
74:   - `nexus.tool.exit_code`: Numeric exit code (for commands/processes)
75:   - `nexus.tool.sandbox`: `bwrap` | `path_confined` | `none`
76:   - `nexus.tool.duration_ms`: Execution duration in milliseconds
77:   - `nexus.tool.error`: Error message if tool failed
78: 
79: #### Compaction Span
80: - **Name:** `nexus.context.compaction`
81: - **Kind:** `INTERNAL`
82: - **Attributes:**
83:   - `nexus.compaction.pre_tokens`: Token count prior to compaction
84:   - `nexus.compaction.post_tokens`: Token count after compaction
85:   - `nexus.compaction.tokens_freed`: Token delta
86:   - `nexus.compaction.preserved_items_count`: Count of active messages retained
87:   - `nexus.compaction.durable_fsync_ms`: Time taken for ordered fsync barrier
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## 3. Credential Redaction & Privacy Pipeline (REQ-DX-105 / CRED003)
92: 
93: Before any span or event is written to disk or memory:
94: 1. **Header Sanitization:** Strip all `Authorization: Bearer ...`, `X-Api-Key: ...`, and `Cookie: ...` headers.
95: 2. **Regex Credential Scanners:** Match and mask common key formats:
96:    - OpenAI (`sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}` → `sk-...[REDACTED]`)
97:    - Anthropic (`sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}` → `sk-ant-...[REDACTED]`)
98:    - GitHub Tokens (`ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}` → `ghp_...[REDACTED]`)
99:    - Private Keys (`-----BEGIN [A-Z ]+ PRIVATE KEY-----` → `[REDACTED PRIVATE KEY]`)
100: 3. **Filesystem Path Preservation:** As specified in `REQ-DX-104`, absolute paths (`/home/user/workspace/file.ts`) are **exempt from redaction** to preserve diagnostic and replay capability.

1: # CRED-003 FlightRecorder Sanitization Evidence
2: 
3: **Starting baseline:** `fc543cab7bb4be3f00993fbbfd148fb11843b16a`
4: **Scope:** CRED-003 durable credential sanitization for flight and audit records.
5: **Status:** Implementation and test evidence; operator acceptance remains pending.
6: 
7: ## Normative contract
8: 
9: Authoritative Phase 2 requirement, `docs/PHASE2_RECONCILED_REQUIREMENTS.md`, Domain 13 — Credential Requirements:
10: 
11: > Credential material MUST be immune from logging, telemetry, and debugging persistence. Crash reports, flight logs, and audit trails MUST scrub all identified credential values prior to disk writes.
12: 
13: Acceptance criterion:
14: 
15: > A crash log or stack trace MUST NOT print active bearer tokens or private keys.
16: 
17: The Phase 3 architecture maps CRED-003 to `InformationFlowBoundary` in INC-06. Phase 4 maps CRED-003 to WP-05 (INC-06), with WP-06/WP-08 listed as dependent packages. The accepted post-WP-05 assessment identified `FlightRecorder` as the known gap: restored tool arguments were persisted in `.nexus/flights/<flightId>.flightlog` without sanitization.
18: 
19: ## Defect reproduction
20: 
21: Before correction, a controlled temporary workspace was used with synthetic bearer, GitHub-style, and OpenAI-style values passed through `FlightRecorder.recordToolCall()`. Reading the resulting `.flightlog` showed all three synthetic plaintext values present (`bearerPersisted=true`, `githubPersisted=true`, `openAiPersisted=true`). No real credentials were used.
22: 
23: ## Correction
24: 
25: `InformationFlowBoundary.redactForTelemetry()` recursively sanitizes string values and object keys in arrays and nested objects, then applies the same canonical classifier over the serialized structure. The second pass preserves contextual classification that depends on a field name and value together. Replacements use the classifier's `[REDACTED:<pattern>]` labels and irreversibly discard plaintext. It does not create reversible token references.
26: 
27: `FlightRecorder.appendEvent()` is the single event persistence boundary. It sanitizes the entire event payload before constructing and appending the JSON line. If classification/sanitization fails, it returns a safe `recordingSkipped` event result without writing that record or propagating classifier diagnostics; authorized local execution continues. Session metadata, prompts, thoughts, tool arguments, result snippets, errors, durable state, diffs, and arbitrary nested payload fields all pass through this boundary.
28: 
29: The separate local audit append in `agent.ts` uses the shared classifier on the complete record, including workspace and tool metadata, arguments, and errors. CRED-003 explicitly names audit trails, and the previous display redactor did not cover all classifier-supported patterns. Sanitization failure is caught by the existing audit-write guard and skips the write.
30: 
31: ## Adversarial and utility evidence
32: 
33: Focused test file: `cli/test/flight_sanitization.test.ts`.
34: 
35: - Before/after disk inspection exercises safe event → sensitive event → safe event appends and parses every JSON line.
36: - Nested arrays and objects contain multiple synthetic credentials, including bearer, GitHub-style, OpenAI-style, and contextual `api_key` values. None survive in the serialized file; matching irreversible redaction markers remain.
37: - Session metadata, model request prompt, thought/reasoning, tool arguments, tool result output snippet, and error fields are checked at the durable artifact.
38: - An authorized WP-05 tokenization/rehydration sequence is dispatched through `AutonomousAgent` under `fullAccess: true`. The registered local capability receives the restored synthetic plaintext and succeeds, while the `.flightlog` contains only the redaction marker. The resulting audit record is read from disk and confirms the credential embedded in the workspace metadata is redacted.
39: - Injected classifier failure during agent dispatch skips flight and audit persistence without blocking the authorized local capability. The capability receives the original synthetic argument, and neither durable file is created.
40: - Non-sensitive paths, notes, call IDs, success state, and neighboring safe records remain materially intact and structurally parseable.
41: 
42: The original implementation had a single `appendFileSync()` in `FlightRecorder`; all record methods route through `appendEvent()`. No alternate FlightRecorder write path was found. Model inputs are represented by turn prompts and session task prompts; reasoning text is recorded as thoughts. Model responses are not stored as raw response bodies. Tool results persist a bounded output snippet and error text, both covered by the common boundary.
43: 
44: ## Validation performed
45: 
46: - Focused CRED-003 tests: 3 passed, 0 failed.
47: - `npm --prefix cli test`: 197 passed, 0 failed; natural exit.
48: - `make test`: Rust tests passed and nested CLI suite reported 197 passed, 0 failed; natural exit.
49: - `npm --prefix cli run build`: passed.
50: - `bash scripts/security_gates.sh`: passed; dependency audits reported zero known vulnerabilities and credential scan reported none in the codebase.
51: - `git diff --check`: passed.
52: 
53: All test credentials are synthetic values constructed in test code. This artifact contains no credential plaintext.
54: 
55: ## Limitations and disposition
56: 
57: This evidence establishes FlightRecorder and the directly named local audit append behavior. It does not claim that every application persistence subsystem is a logging or telemetry sink, nor does it change WP-05 trust ranks, token scoping, rehydration authority, or egress policy. No separate crash-report persistence writer was found in the examined paths; the Phase 2 acceptance criterion for bearer tokens/private keys in crash reports and stack traces remains a bounded limitation pending qualification of all exception-display paths.
58: 
59: CRED-003 is ready for independent qualification and operator review. Issue #12 remains open pending the separate narrow closure reconciliation and operator acceptance.

13: The v1.1.2 release line encompasses two complementary tiers:

17: ### Status in PR #396 (owner decision: connect the new modules or cut them)
18: - **Item 1, connected.** The specialist contracts are runtime roles in `cli/src/core/roles.ts`. An operation unit or `/team` target can run as one. The agent offers only the contract's permitted tools, and it refuses any other call when the call is dispatched (`roleToolAllowList`). That holds whether or not the role is read-only.
19: - **Item 2, connected.** Units with the `reviewer` or `acceptance_reviewer` role run behind the boundary:
20:   - Their prompt is the evidence package: the candidate diff against the operation's base commit, and the verifier receipt of the unit they depend on. Prerequisite summaries are withheld.
21:   - The unit completes only on a well-formed `ACCEPT` that survives the deterministic gates. Prose, a malformed verdict, a reported defect or a failed verifier blocks the unit for an operator decision.
22:   - The verifier receipt comes from the dependency's integration receipt (isolated operations) or, where nothing was integrated (for example `/team`), from the verification recorded on the dependency's completed result. A verification that is not a passing run that executed tests reaches the package as a non-zero exit code. A large (truncated) diff with no passing verifier evidence is rejected.
23:   - Retrying a rejected review resumes the reviewer's conversation. A review unit or read-only specialist (`reviewer`, `acceptance_reviewer`, `semantic_explorer`, `call_site_analyzer`, `security_reviewer`; read-only by construction) does not inherit the write-verification obligation that recovery adds for writer units, since it can neither have written nor run a verifier; writer units, `failure_debugger` (which can run commands) and the read-only `researcher` keep the fail-closed obligation.
24:   - The base a review diffs against is the isolated operation's base commit or, for a non-isolated operation in a Git checkout, the HEAD recorded when the operation first ran (`startCommit`), so a change a unit committed is still in the diff. The base is recorded only before any unit has started; an operation persisted without one, whose work already ran, is never given a base afterwards, and its review blocks. A persisted base is resolved with `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` before use.
25:   - `security_reviewer` is deliberately not behind the boundary: only `reviewer` and `acceptance_reviewer` are. It is a read-only specialist whose contract lists `unified_diff` as an input, and it keeps the ordinary prompt.
26:   - An empty candidate diff is treated as a failure to collect evidence (there is nothing to judge), and the worst verification across all dependencies decides the verifier exit code.
27:   - If the candidate diff cannot be collected (no Git checkout, or the diff exceeds the 4 MiB buffer), the review is blocked before any model turn. That failure is never presented to the reviewer as evidence.
28:   - The runtime package names the real operation id and declares no file scope: no operation or unit declares one, so the scope gate (`detectScopeViolations`) applies only to a package that supplies `authorizedScope`.
29:   - The boundary complements `cli/src/core/independent_check.ts`, which decides whether a verifier pass is independent evidence. It does not replace it.
30: - **Items 3 and 4, cut.** Nothing in the runtime routed on the micro-router. The escalation machine duplicated the non-progress recovery in PR #398, which is connected.
31: - **`TokenBudgetTracker`, cut.** It duplicated `UsageLedger` (`cli/src/usage.ts`), which already enforces `NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_TOKENS` with in-flight reservations.
32: - **Integrated with PR #398.** The recovery context's "Permitted next actions" lists only actions the agent's role and mode allow (`renderRecoveryContext`'s `permits` predicate).
33: - **Item 5 and the CERI and comparative harness entry points are not yet connected.** The throttle needs request latency from `cli/src/client.ts`. CERI needs a `nexus eval` command in `cli/src/index.ts`. Both files are claimed by other open work.

39: ### Item 1: Bounded Specialist Agent Profiles (Workstream A)
40: - **Objective:** Introduce typed specialist profiles with strict tool permissions, input/output contracts, and token budget bounds.
41: - **Existing Capability / Gap:** `ROLE_PROFILES` has 5 untyped text roles. No structured JSON schemas, no granular tool whitelisting beyond binary read-only mode.
42: - **Planned Implementation:**

44:   - Introduce `SpecialistContract`: permitted tools, input requirements, structured output schema, max context tokens, and escalation thresholds.

57: ### Item 2: Objective Independent Review Boundary (Workstream B)
58: - **Objective:** Eliminate reviewer confirmation bias by constructing an objective evidence package stripped of the implementer's narrative claims, enforcing structured review findings.
59: - **Existing Capability / Gap:** Reviewer units currently receive the implementer's summary narrative (`Completed prerequisite work: - <title>: <summary>`), introducing confirmation bias.
60: - **Planned Implementation:**
61:   - Create `cli/src/core/independent_review.ts`.
62:   - Implement `buildReviewEvidencePackage`: extracts objective task requirements, authorized scope, base commit, unified diff, raw verifier receipts, and deliberately omits implementer turn narratives.
63:   - Enforce structured review verdict schema:
64:     ```ts
65:     interface IndependentReviewVerdict {
66:       verdict: "ACCEPT" | "REJECT";
67:       verifiedObservations: string[];
68:       suspectedDefects: Array<{ path: string; line?: number; description: string }>;
69:       unprovenCriteria: string[];
70:       scopeViolations: string[];
71:     }
72:     ```
73:   - Disallow model-generated metrics from establishing authoritative `VERIFIED` status without deterministic verifier evidence.
74: - **Dependencies:** Item 1 (`SpecialistContract`), `cli/src/core/independent_check.ts`.

10:   SOURCE_ROOT=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel)

12:     echo "NEXUS_PACKAGE_SOURCE must be the current Git worktree root" >&2

# Nexus Code v1.1.1

**Maturity:** Stable release for Nexus Code v1.1.1.

This release delivers the complete Nexus Code multi-agent orchestration architecture, serialized git integration with verified execution receipts, typed inter-agent communication, operation replay, and closed edge cases for cancellation idempotency, message durability, prompt submission provenance, and replay envelope protection:
- Multi-agent orchestration with deterministic parallel work units and per-resource slot reservations.
- Serialized Git integration queue with candidate digests and verified execution receipts.
- Typed inter-agent communication channels (`request`, `observation`, `artifact`, `verdict`).
- Operation timeline replay with schema version 2 persistence and safe legacy migration.
- Cancellation idempotency and late result suppression.
- Durability-positive message acknowledgment and structured retry classification.
- Proven prompt submission provenance (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`) protecting message injection against model outputs, tool outputs, and non-Nexus user notes.
- Protected task envelope replay failure propagation across single- and multi-record queries.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.0.0: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js; Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Highlights

### Deterministic parallel work units

An operation may now run more than one work unit at a time:

```json
{
  "objective": "Add a --dry-run flag",
  "policy": { "maxConcurrentUnits": 2 },
  "resources": [
    { "id": "primary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m1" },
    { "id": "secondary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m2", "maxConcurrentUnits": 1 }
  ],
  "units": [
    { "id": "impl", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "docs", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "test", "role": "tester", "dependsOn": ["impl"], "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "review", "role": "reviewer", "dependsOn": ["impl", "test"], "requires": { "independentOf": ["impl"] } }
  ]
}
```

- The scheduler returns an ordered due-set: required units first, then the longest unfinished dependent chain, then the operation's declared unit order. The same persisted state always produces the same due-set.
- Concurrency defaults to **1**. An operation that does not opt in behaves as it did in v1.0.0: one unit in flight.
- Per-resource slots are reserved for the duration of a run, so two units pinned to one single-slot resource serialise. A unit whose qualified slots are busy stays `RUNNABLE` — it is not parked and not escalated.
- One unit's failure does not touch a batch-mate. Cancelling aborts every in-flight unit and leaves each resumable. A restart reconciles every unit that was in flight.

### Retained worktrees are named

A unit worktree with uncommitted or ignored files is kept rather than destroyed, and the event log now says which worktree was kept and why (`WORKTREE_RETAINED`). A clean lifecycle still leaves no unit worktree behind.

# Nexus Code v1.1.2

**Nexus Code v1.1.2** targets the full WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap that was originally planned for v1.1.0. The v1.1.0 release failed and published no release files; v1.1.1 is the published predecessor. Version numbers are immutable, so the roadmap work is assigned to v1.1.2.

## Release scope and status

The intended scope is the complete [WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap](../v1.1.0/ROADMAP.md), together with any already-approved corrective changes needed for the candidate. The operation message-delivery correction described below remains relevant context for the v1.1.1 predecessor.

This document records the target scope; it does not claim that the roadmap is implemented or qualified. As of this note, roadmap implementation and v1.1.2 qualification remain incomplete; completion requires recording the applicable evidence. Work-package completion, exact-head test and type gates, independent review, release-candidate qualification, and publication are still required before v1.1.2 can be called released. Track implementation and evidence in the work-package plans and release qualification record.

## Fixed

### A crash-resumed unit no longer receives a multi-message prompt's later messages twice

When a work unit's prompt carried two or more operator or inter-unit messages, and Nexus stopped after submitting that prompt but before the unit's result was saved, resume recognised only the **first** message as already submitted. Every later message from that prompt was injected into the unit's conversation again.

Resume now recognises each message in a submitted prompt's messages block, whatever its position. Matching is still limited to prompts that Nexus issued (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`, from v1.1.1), so marker text in model output, tool output, or files cannot suppress a message.

- Impact in v1.1.1: the duplicated message was advisory context only. No message was lost, and no `TurnResult`, verification, or acceptance outcome was affected.
- Regression coverage: the post-prompt crash test in `cli/test/operation_release_review.test.ts` now carries two messages. It asserts that each message appears once in the durable history and is acknowledged once.

## Correction to the v1.1.1 notes

The v1.1.1 notes say that a recipient receives undelivered messages "at most once". That holds for prompts carrying a single message. For prompts carrying several messages, v1.1.1 could re-inject the second and later messages after a post-submission crash, as described above. v1.1.2 makes the statement hold in both cases. `docs/releases/v1.1.1.md` carries a matching addendum.

Unchanged from v1.1.1: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js. Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Upgrade

Operation records are unchanged: operation schema version 2, as in v1.1.1. No migration runs, and v1.1.1 can read records written by v1.1.2.

The multi-message resume correction is present in the candidate branch (`c0afc44c`). It is one corrective change within the larger roadmap scope, not the definition of this release. 1: # Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions
2: 
3: These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:
4: 
5: - a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
6: - full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
7: - `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
8: - HEAD moved during a pause.
9: 
10: They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.
11: 
12: ## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent
13: 
14: - The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
15: - An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
16: - An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.
17: 
18: ## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)
19: 
20: Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.
21: 
22: ```sh
23: CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
24: mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
25: SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
26: if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
27:   printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
28:     "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
29: else
30:   echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
31: fi
32: ```
33: 
34: - **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
35: - **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
36: - **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
37: - If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.
38: 
39: ## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes
40: 
41: | Resource | Rule |
42: |---|---|
43: | Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
44: | Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
45: | HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
46: | Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
47: | Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
48: | Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
49: | Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
50: | Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
51: | Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
52: | Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |
53: 
54: ## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly
55: 
56: These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.
57: 
58: | File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
59: |---|---|---|
60: | `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
61: | `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
62: | `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
63: | `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
64: | `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
65: | `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
66: | `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
67: | `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
68: | `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
69: | `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
70: | `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
71: | `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
72: | `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
73: | `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |
74: | `harness.sh`, `install.sh`, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `.github/workflows/*` | 05, 06, 07, 09, C1 | Claim required. Workflow edits are separate commits. |
75: | `cli/dist/**` | all, while tracked | Do not commit `cli/dist` from slices. PLAN-07 PR-7d untracks it (DEC-10). Until that merges, only the merging agent rebuilds and commits dist, in a final separate commit, after rebasing. |
76: | `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md`, `quickstart.md` | 05, 09 and doc tasks in every plan | Edit only the sections your slice changes. Hold a short `FILE_` claim. |
77: 
78: ### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)
79: 
80: A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.
81: 
82: ## 5. Commit and merge discipline
83: 
84: 1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
85: 2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
86: 3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
87: 4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
88: 5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
89: 6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.
90: 
91: ## 6. Coordination records
92:

**Status:** Draft for owner review. **Base:** `main` after the v1.1.2 merge and tag.
**Scope (owner, 2026-11-04):** (1) resolve every open finding from v1.1.2; (2) add Worktrunk functionality in the best-integrated way.

## 1. Principles

- Close findings with the fix first, the regression test red first, and an independent review per work package. Findings are closed with evidence, never by editing the finding.
- No new runtime dependency (gate G1.1-5: zero deprecated packages, `cargo deny`, SBOM, notices). Anything Worktrunk-shaped must be built on Node, git and the system `cp`.

- `/step` is not `cancellable`.
